### Overview

This is the GitHub website for the course **Practical Computing Skills
for Omics Data** (PLNTPTH 5006), a 3-credit course taught at Ohio State
University during the Fall semester of 2026.

The course is taught by [Jelmer Poelstra](mailto:poelstra.1@osu.edu)
from the [CFAES Bioinformatics Core](https://go.osu.edu/bioinformatics-core) and
[Department of Plant Pathology](https://plantpath.osu.edu),
with TA [Kelsey Starr](mailto:starr.320@buckeyemail.osu.edu).

### Course description

Omics data is everywhere, but can you actually analyze it? This course will teach you the skills to do so: using the Unix shell, writing shell and R scripts, and running jobs on the Ohio Supercomputer Center. You will also learn how to improve the reproducibility of your research using best-practice project organization, documentation, and version control. No prior coding experience required.

### Main topics taught

- **Reproducibility** ---
  project documentation with Markdown, file organization, data and management and sharing
- **Unix shell** --- basics, scripting, running command-line programs
- **HPC / Supercomputer ([OSC](https://osc.edu)) usage** ---
  basics, software, and running Slurm batch jobs
- **Version control** --- with Git and GitHub
- **Automated pipelines** --- with Nextflow and nf-core
- **R** --- Basics, data wrangling & visualization, Quarto, and specifics
  to omics data
- **Omics data and analysis basics** ---
  with a focus on high-throughput sequencing data
- **AI** --- Using generative and agentic AI to help with coding
